golden_baseline_location: Output of the legacy parser run through scripts/tp-run-deterministic.sh (TZ=UTC, LC_ALL=C, frozen clock) over the same input files: the pipe-delimited .psv in $ROOT/parsed. Never synthesise a baseline; if the legacy parser cannot run, report recon_result: blocked with the exact command and error.

acceptance_checks.description: Every money column is DECIMAL(14,2) end to end and reconciles exactly to the cent against the source population (T1). A DOUBLE anywhere in a money lineage rejects the PR.

loaded_rows + quarantined_rows == source_rows for every table in the unit, and the quarantine count is reported next to every money figure (T2/T3, §Quarantine). Quarantine above 5% of source rows halts the unit and escalates (STOPA-QUARANTINE).
Rerunning the job with identical inputs produces zero net change: MERGE on the declared key plus ns, proven by a second run whose recon report shows the same row counts and checksums.

Every target row carries ns, every volume path is <ns>/<unit>/..., the job accepts ns as a parameter, and the recon report states the ns it ran under. Nothing unprefixed by ow_tp is read, written or deleted.

BILL-AMT is PIC 9(10)V99 with an implied decimal: value = digits / 100, materialised as DECIMAL(14,2) (D-21). Reading it as an integer inflates money 100x and still looks valid downstream, so recon must compare against the legacy .psv's two-decimal output.

The legacy parser coerces a non-numeric BILL-AMT to 0 via awk's `amt=$4+0`. The target must NOT silently reproduce a zero: such a record is quarantined with reason AMT_NON_NUMERIC and counted, and the divergence from legacy behaviour is stated in the recon report as a deliberate, listed difference.

BILL-DATE is reformatted YYYYMMDD -> YYYY-MM-DD with no validity check in source. An impossible date (e.g. month 13 or 00000000) quarantines the row with reason DATE_INVALID rather than landing as a reformatted string.

HDR and TRL records are excluded from the data population, and the TRL record's count at positions 4-13 is reconciled against the loaded+quarantined count. A mismatch fails the unit: the legacy job only logged it (ETL-0187, never implemented), and that gap is one of the deficiencies this conversion retires.

A file still being written (the legacy ingest has no atomic rename and a lock file it never cleans up) must not be half-loaded: only complete files, identified by a completed transfer marker or a stable size/checksum, are ingested, and idempotency is by file identity plus ns.

planted_anomalies.description: Records whose BILL-AMT is not numeric, coerced to 0 by the legacy parser.
BILL-DATE values that are not real dates.
Files whose TRL count disagrees with the number of detail records.
Records shorter than 65 bytes, which the legacy `cut` pads into empty fields instead of rejecting.

encoding_policy.input_encoding: single-byte ASCII (the legacy parser slices with `cut -c`, which is character-based, so any multibyte byte would shift every downstream column)
encoding_policy.byte_transparency: Slice by byte position 1-65 exactly as the copybook CBCUST01 declares. Do not trim any field except CUST-ID, CUST-NAME and CURRENCY, which the legacy parser trims with `gsub(/ +$/,"",...)`; BILL-DATE, BILL-AMT and REC-TYPE keep their padding, so REC-TYPE comparisons must tolerate it.
encoding_policy.invalid_bytes: A record containing a non-ASCII byte is quarantined with reason ENC_INVALID rather than sliced (D-25), because column positions can no longer be trusted.

malformed_record_policy.details: This is a fixed-width feed, so 'extra fields' means a record longer than 65 bytes: the surplus bytes are captured in a raw_overflow column and the record is flagged, not truncated silently. A record shorter than 65 bytes is quarantined with reason RECORD_SHORT rather than padded, because the legacy parser's padding is indistinguishable from a genuinely blank field. Blank (all-space) fields land as NULL with the reason recorded, never as empty string masquerading as data.

empty_input_semantics.details: No files present is a normal poll outcome, not an error and not an instruction to empty the table: the job no-ops, writes a recon report with files_seen=0, and leaves prior output intact. Deleting prior output on an empty poll would erase earlier batches every quiet interval.
